newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to set tenders for sales of state shares.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to set tenders for sales of state shares.

text.p: The privatisation agency said on Wednesday that an international tender to choose a company to arrange a placement of the state's stake in bank Unibanka, Savings Bank and the Ventspils oil terminal will be held in May.

The agency plans to place abroad some 23 percent of the 33 percent state stake in Unibanka, seven percent of Ventspils Nafta and part of the shares of state-owned firms which have been granted to state-owned Savings Bank to help its balance sheet.
"We planned to organise the tender in May for Unibanka and now we are adding Ventspils and Savings Bank to the list," agency legal director Viktor Shadinov told a news conference.
"The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has agreed that the state stake in Unibanka be reduced to 10 percent," Shadinov added.
The chosen financial intermediary would also place Latvian company shares, worth some eight million lats, included given to Savings Bank's to help boost its balance sheet.
Shares of several state companies, which are on the privatisation list, including Latvenergo, Latvian Shipping, Ventspils Nafta, have been reserved for Savings Bank.
Savings Bank has to buy them for vouchers and sell them on the free market, using the money it makes from the dealings to write-off bad loans and boost its own capital.
